evidence.definition: Total annual emissions of the six greenhouse gases (GHG) covered by the Kyoto Protocol (carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), and sulphurhexafluoride (SF6)) from the energy, industry, waste, and agriculture sectors, standardized to carbon dioxide equivalent values divided by the economy's population. This measure excludes GHG fluxes caused by Land Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF), as these fluxes have larger uncertainties.

claims.text: Who Emits the Most Greenhouse Gases per Person?
claims.support: Indicator EN.GHG.ALL.PC.CE.AR5 measures total annual greenhouse gas emissions per capita.

claims.text: EMISSIONS PER PERSON
A global look at per capita greenhouse gas emissions using World Bank data, from Qatar to DR Congo.
Qatar produces 56.9 tons of greenhouse gases per person. DR Congo produces 0.5.
Kuwait sits right near the top, producing 35.4 tons per person.
Mongolia is a surprise near the peak, producing 29.6 tons per person.
USA produces 17.4 tons per person, 29 times Burundi at 0.6.
Near the bottom, Malawi produces 0.9 tons per person, and Afghanistan just 0.8.
claims.support: Malawi: 0.87847373615846, display 0.9 t; Afghanistan: 0.774601235636553, display 0.8 t
